# `proj yml read`

Load and validate configuration without modifying the project:

```bash
proj yml read [--project <PATH>]
```

The command prints a validation confirmation on success and reports configuration
errors on stderr. It does not dump configuration values; use
[`proj path get`](path.qmd) to query a resolved directory path.

## Configuration and defaults

The base is `_proj.yml`, or the legacy alias `_projr.yml`. Having both is an
error. Active `_projr-<profile>.yml` files override the base, with earlier-listed
profiles winning conflicts. `_projr-local.yml` overrides all active profiles.
Explicit profile selection replaces the environment list. Profile/local filename
aliases are separate from the implemented base alias.

Read-only queries accept missing configuration as an empty directory inventory.
Builds require an active base or explicitly activated profile at the root.
Inactive profiles and local overrides alone do not qualify. Every declared
directory requires an explicit nonempty path; missing labels are never invented.
Unsupported control fields fail validation; `metadata` and `parameters` remain
arbitrary maps. Parameter aliases normalize before merging; conflicting aliases
within one file are rejected. No query writes defaults into configuration.

`proj --project . --non-interactive init directories` creates a missing base with
explicit `_raw_data`, `_tmp` and `_output` paths. It creates declared directories
and synchronizes ignore rules without Git/GitHub setup. Existing configuration
bytes are preserved. It leaves scripts absent, preserving discovery; `scripts: []`
continues to mean no analysis.

Configuration validation and path queries do not change `.gitignore`,
`.Rbuildignore`, configuration files, or project directories. Production builds
and directory initialization request ignore synchronization explicitly.
Directory initialization stops on configuration read/validation errors before
changing ignore rules or creating directories.


## Read configuration values and analysis parameters

The existing yml read command still reports validation only. These commands
return the requested values; that data can include private configuration
values, so do not publish their output as a diagnostic log.

~~~bash
proj --machine yml get --check
proj --machine yml get --profile team
proj --machine yml parameter model seed
proj --machine yml parameter -- --literal-key
~~~

The result keys are configuration and value respectively. Empty parameter selectors
return the whole parameter value; absent keys return null. Keys are literal mapping
keys, not R expressions, dotted-path evaluation or array indexes. Existing four
shared parameter aliases normalize per layer before merging. Parameter queries
apply runtime validation; get applies it only with --check. Unchecked get still
requires a mapping and rejects malformed or conflicting aliases.

CLI profile flags select merged overlays. Without an explicit profile, queries
inside a build retain its captured profile order for that project. Configuration
contents are read at query time; fingerprints do not freeze every analysis input.
Explicit project overrides retain their existing behavior. No directories, ignore
rules, dependency installation or build records are created by these queries.
